title: Project report
status: How a project report for a term loan with working capital is worked out here, in the form chartered accountants commonly use for small and medium enterprises. Set by Claude at the owner's request (02-10-2026); the depreciation rates and the working-capital methods are as described in public sources, not checked against the primary texts from here.
depreciationSource: Written-down value at the income-tax rates (Income-tax Rules, 1962, Appendix I): buildings 10%, plant and machinery 15%, furniture 10%; other fixed assets and the contingency on them at the plant-and-machinery rate. A full year's depreciation in the first year.

workingCapital.worked: Worked out, the lower of the two on the first year of sales at its full rate: 75% of its stock and debtors less its creditors (the need), and the bank's 20% of its sales (the turnover method)
workingCapital.source: The second method of lending (Tandon Committee): the bank finances up to 75% of current assets, less creditors. The turnover method for small enterprises (Nayak Committee, RBI): working capital of 25% of the year's sales, of which the bank finances 20%.

costHeads.note: Costs by head in expert mode (the owner's list, 21-10-2026, D-UX-112): those that vary with sales as a % of sales, the rest in rupees a month, growing together; each named in the profit and loss

assumptions.what: The rest of the cost of the project
assumptions.shown: None: no land, furniture, other fixed assets, contingency or preliminary expenses
assumptions.why: Type them in expert mode if the project has them

assumptions.shown: No capital subsidy and no unsecured loans
assumptions.why: Type them in expert mode if the project has them

assumptions.shown: First drawn this month, repaid by EMI every month
assumptions.why: The usual for a term loan; type the month and the way it is repaid in expert mode

assumptions.shown: Until the month you start selling
assumptions.why: The owner's rule (D-UX-112): no instalment before the first sales; a lender may give more
On the careful side: costs rise each year while the price is held where it is
Banks often price the two alike; type the sanction's rate in expert mode

assumptions.shown: 30 days each: stock and creditors of the year's materials and other variable costs, debtors of the year's sales
assumptions.why: A common level for a small business; type the business's own

assumptions.shown: Fully used from the first sales, and its interest paid, in every year
assumptions.why: On the careful side: more interest, lower profit

assumptions.shown: None: the profits stay in the business
assumptions.why: Type them in the figures if the owners take money out

assumptions.shown: Paid in the year it falls due
assumptions.why: No tax is left owing in the balance sheet

assumptions.shown: 60% in the first year of sales, 70% in the second, 80% from the third
assumptions.why: A new unit rarely runs full at once; type the business's own in expert mode

assumptions.shown: Held where it is in every year
assumptions.why: On the careful side: sales grow only with the use of the capacity

assumptions.shown: Paid by the borrower every year, at the scheme's rate, as a finance cost
assumptions.why: The bank may bear it, pass it on or add a risk-based fee; type the sanction letter's rate in expert mode (0 if the bank bears it)

assumptions.shown: Pro rata by months: the term loan's from its first draw, the limit's from the first sales
assumptions.why: The schemes bill the first year for twelve months or to 31 March; by months, each year bears its own part

assumptions.shown: None: the fee's slab is set by this term loan and limit alone
assumptions.why: Other loans the borrower has under CGTMSE add to the cover and may raise the slab; type the sanction letter's rate if so

assumptions.shown: The standard rate for the slab, less the concessions ticked
assumptions.why: A bank's own rate may be up to 10% lower or 70% higher; type the sanction letter's rate in expert mode
The upper figure: the bank reports the outstanding it expects, which may be less

assumptions.shown: Counted in the term loan outstanding until it is set off after 3 years
assumptions.why: The upper figure: the bank holds it as a deposit against the loan until then

pmegp.label: PMEGP (Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme)
pmegp.notice: Fresh PMEGP applications are paused until the scheme is continued with revised guidelines (the PMEGP portal, October 2026); the figures here are the 2021-22 to 2025-26 guideline's and may change. The Rajya Sabha committee on industry recommended raising the Rs. 50 lakh manufacturing ceiling (report of 11-03-2026, pib.gov.in PRID 2238242).
pmegp.source: PMEGP guidelines as revised by the Ministry of MSME's O.M. PMEGP/UdhyamReg./01/2023 of 07-12-2023 (docs/inbox/pmegp-guidelines-2023-12-07.pdf, read 20-10-2026), which supersedes the certified 2022 text (KVIC, https://www.kvic.gov.in/kvicres/update/pmegp/PMEGP_Guidelines_Certified_2022.pdf) with the same figures and adds Udyam registration before the margin money is adjusted: para 3.1 and its notes (shares and ceilings), 4.1 (land, education, existing units), 8.1 and 8.3 (the bank's share, working capital), 11.20 (the deposit). The guideline covers 2021-22 to 2025-26; no notice continuing it into 2026-27 was found on kvic.gov.in, and kviconline.gov.in does not answer this cloud
rules: The margin money (subsidy) is a share of the project cost: 15% in a town and 25% in a village for the general category; 25% and 35% for the special categories.

The project cost leaves out the land and includes the working capital; the subsidy is worked on at most Rs. 50 lakh for manufacturing and Rs. 20 lakh for a service, and the bank may lend above that without subsidy.
The borrower brings at least 10% of the project cost (5% for the special categories); the working capital is at most 40% of the project cost for manufacturing and 60% for a service.

Above Rs. 10 lakh in manufacturing or Rs. 5 lakh in a service, the borrower must have passed class VIII. Only new units can apply: not an existing unit, nor one that has had a government subsidy under another scheme.

The margin money is kept as a deposit for 3 years: no interest is paid on it and none is charged on the same amount of the loan; after 3 years it is set off against the loan, once the unit is verified.
pmegp.ours: The instalments are worked on the loan less the margin money, so the deposit clears that part of the loan when it is set off; ask the bank how it fixes them.
conditions: The project buys fixed assets: one without capital expenditure cannot be financed.
A ready-built, leased or rented shed counts in the project cost for at most 3 years.

Trading only as a sales outlet in the North-East, a district affected by left-wing extremism or the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, or selling Khadi, village-industry or PMEGP products, or backed by the unit's own manufacturing or service.
Only one person from a family (self and spouse) is financed under PMEGP.
The unit is registered on the Udyam portal before it is verified and the margin money is set off.
pmegp.conditionsSource: PMEGP guidelines as revised on 07-12-2023, para 4.1 (ii) to (vi) and its note (docs/inbox/pmegp-guidelines-2023-12-07.pdf, read 21-10-2026).

mudra.label: Mudra (Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana)
mudra.source: MUDRA's Offerings page (mudra.org.in, saved 20-10-2026: docs/inbox/mudra-offerings-2026-10-20.pdf): Shishu up to Rs. 50,000, Kishor above 50,000 and up to 5 lakh, Tarun above 5 lakh and up to 10 lakh, Tarun Plus above 10 lakh and up to 20 lakh; a term loan and working capital up to 20 lakh a unit; loans up to 20 lakh collateral free, guaranteed by CGFMU, run by NCGTC. Tarun Plus only for those who have availed and repaid a Tarun loan: S.O. 4658(E) of 24-10-2024 (docs/inbox/cgfmu-tarun-plus-so4658-2024-10-24.pdf). JanSamarth as the portal for Mudra loans, with this address: PIB's explainer of 08-04-2026 (docs/inbox/mudra-pib-explainer-2026-04-08.pdf).
rules: Mudra is a loan, not a subsidy: up to Rs. 20 lakh in all, the term loan and the working-capital limit together, at the bank's own rate of interest.
Its level is by the amount: Shishu up to Rs. 50,000, Kishor up to Rs. 5 lakh, Tarun up to Rs. 10 lakh, and Tarun Plus up to Rs. 20 lakh, only for a borrower who has repaid a Tarun loan.
No collateral is needed: the loan is guaranteed by CGFMU (the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units), run by NCGTC.

cgfmu.label: CGFMU (the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units), run by NCGTC
cgfmu.source: CGFMU's FAQ of 18-02-2025, Q14 (docs/inbox/cgfmu-faq-2025-02-18.pdf): from 01-04-2023, the base year at 1% a year of the sanctioned amount, later years on the amount outstanding on 1 April, a working-capital account on its sanctioned amount every year; the bank may recover it from the borrower. The scheme charges the base year 'for the full year or the broken period i.e. till March 31' (S.O. 1443(E) of 18-04-2016, para 8(i)(a): docs/inbox/cgfmu-scheme-so1443-2016-04-18.pdf), worked here pro rata by months (the owner, 21-10-2026).

cgtmse.label: CGTMSE (the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises)
groups: A woman, SC or ST promoter, a person with a disability, an Agniveer or a transgender person
In the North-East, Jammu and Kashmir or Ladakh (loans up to Rs. 50 lakh), or an aspirational or credit-deficient district
cgtmse.source: CGTMSE's Fee Structure page and CGS-I as updated on 01-04-2026, para 8 and 8.1 and Annexure II (docs/inbox/cgtmse-fee-structure.pdf, docs/inbox/cgtmse-scheme-cgs1-2026-04-01.pdf): a standard rate a year by slab of the unit's whole cover, on the amount guaranteed for the first year, then on a term loan's outstanding at 31 December and a working-capital limit's present or expected outstanding; 10% off for each group, the concession taken first and rounded to two decimals; each bank pays 10% less or up to 70% more by its claims record, and may pass the fee on. CGTMSE's FAQ on the fee, Q6 (docs/inbox/cgtmse-faq-agf.pdf): the first fee for a year, the next pro rata to 31 March.

method: Sales are the capacity × its use × the price a unit (or the sales typed, growing by the percentage given), for the months after sales start in the first year; fixed costs likewise, growing by the percentage given; materials and other variable costs are the same share of sales every year.
Profit before interest, depreciation and tax is sales less variable and fixed costs. Depreciation is on the written-down value; preliminary expenses are written off in five equal parts.
Interest on the term loan is from its repayment schedule; interest on working capital is the limit × its rate. Tax is worked out by who the borrower is.

Stock, debtors and creditors are the days given of a full year's figures at that year's rate, even in a first year of a few months. The margin for working capital, part of the cost of the project, is what the first year's stock and debtors need beyond the creditors and the bank's limit.
The promoters bring in the cost of the project less the term loan, any subsidy and any unsecured loans.
Cash in hand is what the cash flow leaves; the balance sheet must balance with it, or no figures are shown.

DSCR is the common term-loan DSCR: (profit after tax + depreciation + preliminary expenses written off + interest on the term loan) ÷ (principal + interest on the term loan); the average is the totals' ratio.

Break-even: fixed costs (with depreciation, preliminary expenses written off interest and any guarantee fee) ÷ the contribution (sales less variable costs), as a share of sales; the cash break-even leaves out depreciation and the write-off.

A guarantee fee, when the loans are guaranteed (CGFMU under Mudra, or CGTMSE when ticked), is a finance cost, worked a month at a time. CGFMU: 1% a year of the term loan sanctioned in the year of its first draw, then of what is outstanding on 1 April, and of the working-capital limit. CGTMSE: the rate for the slab of the whole cover, less 10% for each concession ticked; on the amount guaranteed for the first twelve months, then on what was outstanding on the 31 December before each year, while the loan runs; and on the whole limit. The fee before the first sales is paid from the cost of the project, with the interest then.
